title: Assignment 8: Turn Toward the Open Side with ROS 2
description: Use the four obstacle distances on /flbr to drive straight when the way is clear, and otherwise stop and turn toward the side with more space.
assignment_html:
Scenario

In Assignment 1 your robot stopped in front of a wall. Now it should keep going: drive forward while the way ahead is clear, and when something is close in front, stop and turn toward the side with more space. The robot never stops for good; it keeps finding a new way forward.

What the robot gives you

  • The robot's laser is already summarised for you. A helper node turns every scan into four numbers and publishes them on /flbr as rse_msgs/msg/Flbr, about 12 times per second: msg.front, msg.left, msg.back and msg.right.
  • Each number is the distance in metres to the closest obstacle in that direction (a 90° slice centred on front, left, back or right).
  • A distance can be NaN (not a number) when that direction has no usable reading. Treat NaN as no space (0.0): never drive toward an unknown front, and never turn toward an unknown side when the other side is known. math.isnan(value) tells you when a distance is NaN.
  • /cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/msg/Twist) moves the robot. linear.x is the forward speed in m/s; angular.z is the turn speed in rad/s. Positive angular.z turns left, negative turns right.

The rule your node must follow (for every /flbr message)

  • Front clear (front greater than 0.75 m): drive straight, linear.x = 0.20 and angular.z = 0.0.
  • Front blocked (front 0.75 m or less, or NaN): linear.x = 0.0 and turn on the spot toward the side with more space: angular.z = +0.5 (left) when left is greater than right, otherwise angular.z = -0.5 (right). This also covers a tie and the case where both sides are unknown (both 0.0): turn right.
  • The back distance is there if you want to print it, but the rule does not use it.

Press Simulate to watch your node drive a robot around a small room with a box in it. The simulation is only for watching: it does not change your score.

Task

Complete the TODOs in src/open_side/open_side/controller.py:

  1. Create a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel with queue depth 10.
  2. Subscribe to Flbr messages on /flbr with queue depth 10, calling self.handle_flbr.
  3. In handle_flbr, read msg.front, msg.left and msg.right, using 0.0 for any NaN.
  4. Drive straight when the front is clear; otherwise stop and turn toward the side with more space. Use self.forward_speed, self.turn_speed and self.stop_distance.
  5. Publish exactly one Twist for each message.

Rules

  • Read the complete project tree, but edit only src/open_side/open_side/controller.py.
  • Do not rename the package, executable, node, topics, class or handle_flbr, and keep main() as it is.
  • controller.py may import only rclpy, geometry_msgs, rse_msgs and math.
  • Do not use a while True loop or sleep(): let the callback do the work.

What Run Tests checks

The grader sends your node made-up /flbr messages and watches /cmd_vel. No robot simulator is used. Each situation lasts 0.8 seconds (about 10 messages), and every command is checked against the message that triggered it. The situations, in order:

  • Front 2.0 m: drive straight.
  • Front 2.0 m, much more space on the left: still drive straight (do not turn while clear).
  • Front 0.5 m, more space on the left: stop and turn left.
  • Front 0.5 m, more space on the right: stop and turn right.
  • Front exactly 0.75 m: blocked, so stop and turn.
  • Front 0.5 m, left and right equal: stop and turn right.
  • Front unknown (NaN): stop and turn.
  • Front 0.5 m, right unknown (NaN): stop and turn left, never toward the unknown side.
  • Front 2.0 m again: drive straight again.

Drive straight means linear.x within ±0.02 of 0.20 m/s and angular.z within ±0.001. Stopped means linear.x within ±0.001. Turning means angular.z within ±0.05 of +0.5 or -0.5. All other Twist fields must stay 0.0. Stopping and turning only earn credit when the robot also drives when the front is clear.

This is a test with made-up distances, not a real-robot safety certification.

How scoring works

Each check has points. The build and start checks count once your own code passes at least one behaviour check, so the untouched starter earns 0%. The task counts as passed when every check passes.

from rclpy.executors import ExternalShutdownException
from rclpy.node import Node
from rse_msgs.msg import Flbr


class OpenSideController(Node):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('open_side_controller')

        # TODO 1: Create a Twist publisher on /cmd_vel with queue depth 10.
        self.velocity_publisher = None

        # TODO 2: Subscribe to Flbr messages on /flbr with queue depth 10,
        # and call self.handle_flbr for each message.
        self.flbr_subscription = None

        self.forward_speed = 0.20   # m/s
        self.turn_speed = 0.5       # rad/s
        self.stop_distance = 0.75   # m

    def handle_flbr(self, msg):
        # TODO 3: Read msg.front, msg.left and msg.right. A NaN distance is
        # unknown: treat it as no space (0.0). math.isnan() tells you when.

        command = Twist()
        # TODO 4: If the front is greater than self.stop_distance, drive
        # straight: set command.linear.x to self.forward_speed.
        # TODO 5: Otherwise keep linear.x at 0.0 and turn toward the side
        # with more space: +self.turn_speed (left) when left > right,
        # otherwise -self.turn_speed (right).
        pass

        # TODO 6: Publish the velocity command.
        pass


def main(args=None):
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    controller = OpenSideController()
    try:
        rclpy.spin(controller)
    except (KeyboardInterrupt, ExternalShutdownException):
        pass
    finally:
        controller.destroy_node()
        rclpy.try_shutdown()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

solution_html:
Approach

  1. Create the Twist publisher on /cmd_vel and the Flbr subscription on /flbr, both with queue depth 10.
  2. In the callback, replace a NaN front, left or right with 0.0 (no space).
  3. If the front is greater than stop_distance, publish linear.x = forward_speed with angular.z = 0.0.
  4. Otherwise publish linear.x = 0.0 and angular.z = +turn_speed when left is greater than right, or -turn_speed otherwise.
  5. Publish exactly one command per message, so the robot reacts to every new reading.
